overview.description: As-Nas is a historical Persian vying game played with a small five-suit pack, using poker-like betting and ranked combinations before modern poker standardized.

history.origins: As-Nas was played in Persia with dedicated illustrated cards and is often discussed as part of the broader family of early vying games that predate or parallel poker.
timeline: 19th century: As-Nas cards and game play are documented in Persia.
Modern era: The game survives mainly as a historical card-game form.
history.cultural: As-Nas is included because it has a distinct play system rather than being only a title or expansion page.

nullReasons.evolution: No detailed evolution chain is documented beyond the described form and listed variants.

setup.players: Two to five players can take part in a betting round.
setup.deck: Use the traditional As-Nas pack, commonly twenty cards with five copies of ranked court-style cards.
setup.equipment: Traditional 20 or 25-card As-Nas pack, score area, and enough table space for play.
setup.dealing: Deal a small hand to each player, then conduct betting rounds around the table.

rules.objective: Win the pot either by holding the strongest ranked hand at showdown or by causing all opponents to fold.
rules.gameplay: Players receive hidden cards and bet on the strength of their combinations. Calling leads to comparison of ranked hands; folding concedes the pot. The small deck makes rank frequency and opponent behavior central.
keyRules: Uses a dedicated Persian As-Nas pack.
Players bet, call, raise, or fold around hidden hands.
Best ranked hand wins at showdown.
A player can win uncontested if all others fold.
